title: P24: MLP expansion 4x -> 5x (d_ff 1024 -> 1280) in all six blocks (5.58M params) on the 101-claude Lean incumbent
description: P24 (more MLP capacity): widen every block's MLP from 4x to 5x d_model (d_ff 1024 -> 1280), the only edit to 101-claude's pretrain.py, giving 5,581,824 params, within 1,792 of 102-claude's seven-block 5,583,616 at the same matmul FLOPs per token but at depth 6. 102's seventh block lost -37 with equal round-1 RL accuracy but slower later rounds; if that came from the extra sequential layer rather than the extra parameters, spending the same parameters on symbol-transforming MLP width should give expert iteration more correct long Lean proofs.
hypothesis: At d_model 256 the pretraining step and every RL decode step look dominated by per-layer cost (100/101/102 took ~4,330/3,600/3,100 steps, in proportion to 1/depth), so widening the MLPs should cost fewer steps than adding a block. Lean have-chains apply connective rules to nested formulas, a per-token symbol transformation that lives in the MLPs, and val loss plateaus by ~135 s of the 300 s pretraining, so there is step budget to spend on MLP capacity. If 102's loss was caused by the seventh sequential layer rather than its 0.79M extra parameters, this parameter- and FLOP-matched wide-MLP model keeps 101's depth and RL adaptation speed while adding capacity and scores above 580; if extra parameters themselves slow the fixed AdamW RL rounds, it lands near 102's 542.
expected_delta: -35 to +35 dev solves >= 7 vs 580 (central 0); pretraining ~3,250-3,550 steps vs 3,573-3,624 (102: 3,087-3,114), final val loss 0.078-0.085, round-4 RL sample acc at or above 102's 0.63-0.65, RL sampling ~175-225 samples/s, totals ~1,850-2,050 s (no timeout expected)

arch.change: CHANGED vs 101-claude: D_FF 1024 -> 1280 (MLP expansion 4x -> 5x) in all six blocks; the fork's Block hardcodes 4*d, so pretrain() replaces each block's fc1/fc2 with nn.Linear(256,1280)/nn.Linear(1280,256) (biases zeroed) before moving the model to the device; everything else identical
arch.n_params_detail: 6 blocks 5,526,528 (921,088 each: qkv 197,376 + proj 65,792 + fc1 328,960 + fc2 327,936 + 2 LayerNorms 1,024) + emb 27,392 + head 27,392 + ln_f 512 = 5,581,824 (vocab 107); 102-claude's seven 4x blocks had 5,583,616, so the two differ by 1,792 params and match in matmul FLOPs per token (6*(4+10) = 7*(4+8) d^2)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from the fork, then every block's fc1/fc2 swapped for width-1280 Linears; model.cfg does not record d_ff, so the fork's load_ckpt alone cannot rebuild it. The harness fine-tunes and samples the returned module directly
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per block (6 per sample), unchanged fork attention; CPU check: token-by-token cached decode matches the full forward to 1.2e-7 (random weights, width-1280 MLPs)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched rule unchanged from 078-claude): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 and fc2 sqrt(5) = 2.24 (101-claude: 2), head (107,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 24 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 6 blocks) plus head.weight (107,256; no bias) are in Muon: 25 matrices. Six qkv.weight (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates as a batch of three (256,256); proj (256,256), fc1 (1280,256), fc2 (256,1280) and head are orthogonalized whole (tall ones transposed). fc1 is not mistaken for QKV by the (3D, D) shape test since 1280 != 768
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Same rule as 101-claude: fork default construction, each block's fc1/fc2 replaced by fresh nn.Linear(256,1280)/nn.Linear(1280,256) with zeroed biases, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), element RMS 0.02); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02). The replacement layers' construction draws shift the global RNG stream relative to 101-claude.
